articles.title: FC Barcelona eyes €300 million and more in annual retail revenue under record Nike partnership until 2038
articles.summary: FC Barcelona is currently aiming to generate more than €300 million pounds per season from its retail and licensing business as part of its expanded
articles.body: FC Barcelona is currently aiming to generate more than €300 million pounds per season from its retail and licensing business as part of its expanded partnership with Nike. The ambitious target forms the club's long-term strategy to boost its commercial operation, expand its global reach, and increase its revenue from Nike's merchandise sales.As per reports, Barcelona announced its renewed strategic partnership with Nike in November 2024, describing it as a new beginning of a relationship that began in 1998. The agreement was subsequently ratified by the club members in December 2024, and again it became effective from the 2024-25 season.It is to be noted that this agreement is the largest sponsorship deal in its history. According to Fabrizio Romano, the president of Barcelona, he stated, “The new contract with Nike is 3x more valuable than the previous one. It’s the biggest contract in football world for technical sponsor partnership.”FC Barcelona aims to expand retail and licensing revenue to €300 million with their partner NikeFC Barcelona and Nike have renewed a strategic alliance to ensure the global development of the Club's Retail and Licensing business. According to earlier reports, Barcelona has set an initial target of reaching €200 million per season in retail and licensing revenue before exceeding €300 million in the medium term.Also, under the renewed arrangement, Nike will work alongside Barça Licensing & Merchandising (BLM), the club’s subsidiary responsible for licensing and merchandising, to develop products, improve supply-chain operations and strengthen global distribution.The agreement between FC Barcelona and Nike is structured in three main strategic areas are sponsorship rights, product licensing, and support for retail and eCommerce operations. Basically, the contract allows Barcelona to develop its own branded merchandise and pursue strategic partnerships with brands outside Nike’s competing technical-product category.In February 2026, Barcelona reported that UEFA’s annual club report had placed its kit and merchandising revenue at a record €277 million, €46 million ahead of the second-ranked club. Barcelona credited its renewed Nike partnership and the expansion of its retail and e-commerce operations as important factors behind that growth. Even the increase in revenue was reported well above the industry average, with indicators that double or even triple typical market standards.The €300 million target therefore represents a further step in Barcelona’s ambition to maximise the value of its global brand. However, the growth will depend on the increased sales of the official merchandise, international retail expansion and the club’s ability to convert its worldwide fan base into commercial growth.With Nike’s long-term partnership, Barcelona will look to build on its existing merchandising business and establish retail and licensing as an increasingly significant source of recurring revenue.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Big 10 Pick 6: Bring to a Gentle Boil
articles.summary: I went 0-6 against the spread two weeks ago and bounced back to 5-1 last week, missing on the crazy Minnesota letdown against Purdue. That brings me near eve...
articles.body:
I went 0-6 against the spread two weeks ago and bounced back to 5-1 last week, missing on the crazy Minnesota letdown against Purdue. That brings me near even at 17-19 ATS on the year. Another good week can get me back in the black, so let's get straight to the picks.

Before the season, the idea that the Dawgs would be underdogs in this game would have seemed unfathomable. The Huskies were ranked #17 in the country and Purdue hadn't won a conference game roughly since Joe Tiller and Drew Brees played in West Lafayette. Now, the Boilermakers have won two in a row (that's a streak!) against Illinois and Minnesota- the very same Gophers team that pantsed UW at home in the conference opener. They have excelled on the back of Fami Ijeboi, a Minnesota transfer who has run 40 times for 260 yards over the last two weeks. QB Ryan Brown has shown growth, already matching last year's 9 TD passes, but doing it against a single Int after tossing 10 of them a year ago. The Husky defense absolutely must revert to their early-season form and leave last week's missed tackles and assignments in the rearview.

Of course, the more interesting question is what UW's offense will look like. While Purdue's defense has got the job done thus far in conference play, they still rank only 104th nationally in defensive SP+. Notre Dame, UCLA, and Wake Forest averaged over 40 ppg against them in their three losses. Washington's rush offense has been DOA most of the year with sub-par blocking and RB depth that was never supposed to be forced into regular action this year. However, Demond Williams' rib injury last week brough Elijah Brown in at QB and he immediately showed better timing and an ability to read the defense that brought the passing game to life. Was Brown's success a mirage against an Iowa defense that let its foot off the pedal with a big lead? Will he backslide against a defense that spent the week preparing for him? Above all, Brown has to play within himself and avoid turnovers. Purdue has surged by avoiding turnovers and UW doesn't have enough margin for error to lose the turnover differential. Maybe I'm just looking at this game through rose-colored glasses because I can't imagine UW losing out and this looks like the best chance to win a B1G game, but I feel relatively optimistic this week.

Indiana's winning streak very nearly came to a halt last week against Nebraska. They escaped, but the task ahead only gets tougher. Despite their season-opening loss in Austin, Ohio St is #1 in the country by SP+ (for their part, Indiana is 5th). Ohio St has defended the run very well this year, which could force Josh Hoover to do more against a great secondary than he has had to do most of the year. A big theme of Indiana's win last season in the B1G Championship Game was the pass rush, and Ohio St has questions about their own OL health. The game should be close, so I'm going to side with Jeremiah Smith, the best player in the country.

Northwestern has been one of the best stories of the season so far, at 4-1 with their only loss a close one to Indiana. Pat Fitzgerald will face Northwestern as a HC for the first time, and Aidan Chiles will start at QB for the Cats after going in the opposite direction. Northwestern runs the ball well, especially with RB Caleb Komolafe, while the Spartans do not defend it well. Michigan St will likely be able to move the ball and whether the game stays close will depend on whether Northwestern can force negative plays and red zone stops as they have all year.

The amazing thing about this game is that somebody has to win. Michigan has lost their last two (and would be 2-3 but for that wild ending to open the year against Western Michigan). Penn St has dropped three in a row and does not look ready to compete in the B1G. Michigan's struggles have bee mostly isolated to the offensive side and their run defense has been legitimately good. Penn St likes to play offense in a phone booth, so this game could get ugly. Michigan turns the ball over too much and struggles to pass consistently. The game should be low-scoring, which makes me lean toward the underdog.

Dylan Raiola probably didn't expect to start this game when he transferred from Nebraska to Oregon. However, he probably had that expectation because he thought he'd be backing up Dante Moore, not because he'd be coming off his worst game of the season (6/19, 43 yards, 3 turnovers). There is no confirmation yet, but it sounds like Brock Thomas is more likely to get the first crack. Nebraska's defense has been consistently solid under Matt Ruhle. The offense has generally looked better this year with OC Dana Holgerson and QB Anthony Colandrea. Even coming off a home loss, I think Autzen gives the Ducks an edge, but this game could go either way.

Even at 4-1, there is reason to remain skeptical of the Badgers. Their win over Penn St looks less impressive than it did at the time, and the rest of their victories have been against softer parts of the schedule. UCLA lost QB Nico Iamaleava for the year during the Oregon game and will likely use Ty Dieffnbach in his place. Regardless of who plays QB, Bob Chesney prefers to run the ball and the Bruins have done that well. Wisconsin is good against the run, but I'm not sure they're good enough to stymie Wayne Knight and company. UCLA leads then nation in takeaways and Wisconsin QB Colton Joseph has already thrown 5 picks. If Wisconsin can be neutral or better in turnovers, they can keep it close, but that might be asking a lot.

articles.title: Led by Angel Reese, six WNBA Finals competitors headline the 2026 All-Defensive First and Second Teams
articles.summary: Both the Dream and Valkyries put three players on the 2026 All-Defensive Teams.
articles.body:
If there needed to be more evidence that defense will define these WNBA Finals, the 2026 WNBA All-Defensive Teams provided it, as three members of the Atlanta Dream and three members of the Golden State Valkyries combined to claim six of the 10 spots.

Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese headlines the All-Defensive First Team, where she is joined by Dream teammate Rhyne Howard. Jordin Canada was elected to the Second Team.

Gabby Williams, the Defensive Player of the Year runner up, secured a spot on the First Team, and two Valkyries, Veronica Burton and Kiah Stokes, represent Golden State on the Second Team.

The All-Defensive selection is a first for Reese. Both Howard and Burton earn their second-straight and second-overall defensive honors, while Stokes, after a more than decade gap, receives her second All-Defensive nomination, with her first earned in 2015 as member of the New York Liberty. Williams and Canada are now three-time All-Defensive honorees. Williams, then with the Seattle Storm, was awarded in 2022 and 2025; Canada got the nods in 2019 with the Storm and in 2023 with the Los Angeles Sparks.

Filling out the First Team alongside Reese, Howard and Williams were the Las Vegas Aces' A'ja Wilson and Washington Mystics' Shakira Austin. It's the sixth All-Defensive selection for the three-time Defensive Player of the Year Wilson, whereas Austin is a first-time nominee.

Austin's Mystics teammate, Sonia Citron, also earned her first All-Defensive award as a member of the Second Team. Rounding out the Second Team of Canada, Burton, Stokes and Citron is Breanna Stewart, with this marking the eighth All-Defensive award for the Liberty stalwart.

articles.title: Texas’ Arch Manning Urged to Make Bold Indiana Move Amid Heisman Talk
articles.summary: One analyst believes a change in offensive systems could completely change Manning's future, pointing to Indiana's success with transfer quarterbacks. The po...
articles.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning entered the season facing enormous expectations, but another uneven stretch from the Longhorns has raised questions about whether the offense is getting the most out of him.

Following Saturday's 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, Manning has thrown 10 touchdowns and five interceptions through five games. Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian has defended his quarterback, although the problems haven't been limited to Manning's mistakes.

Now, one college football analyst believes what may need to happen for the former five-star quarterback to reach his full potential is to make a transfer.

RJ Young Predicts Arch Manning Heisman Win at Indiana

FOX Sports' RJ Young argued that the responsibility for Texas' offensive struggles belongs more to its head coach than its quarterback.

"Texas doesn't have an Arch Manning problem. It has a Steve Sarkisian play-calling problem," Young wrote.

He then made a bold prediction about what Manning might accomplish in a different offense.

"Arch wins the Heisman Trophy if transfers to Indiana in 2027," Young wrote.

To be clear, Young wasn't suggesting that a transfer is in motion. There has been no reported decision by Manning to enter the portal, and nothing indicating Indiana is recruiting him. The comment was a what-if about the impact of coaching and offensive structure.

Young's example was Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover, who transferred from TCU following the 2025 season. The numbers behind his point are compelling.

"Josh Hoover threw 33 INTs in 35 games at TCU. At IU, he's rocking 17 TDs and 0 picks on the stat sheet," Young wrote.

Hoover has thrown for 1,364 yards with 17 touchdowns and no interceptions through six games, helping Indiana start 6-0. Across his final three seasons at TCU, he threw 33 interceptions in 35 appearances.

The comparison doesn't guarantee Manning would have the same results. But it does provide a reason to wonder what he might look like playing for Curt Cignetti.

Indiana's Quarterback Success Adds Intrigue to Arch Manning Idea

Cignetti has already helped one transfer quarterback reach the sport's highest individual honor. Fernando Mendoza arrived from California, won the 2025 Heisman Trophy and led Indiana to a 16-0 national championship season.

Hoover has kept the Hoosiers rolling in 2026, and his improvement in protecting the football only strengthens Young's argument about the coaching environment. Indiana has found a way to get strong production from two quarterbacks with vastly different backgrounds.

Texas, meanwhile, is coming off a loss in which Manning threw for 260 yards and three touchdowns but also had two fourth-quarter interceptions. The Longhorns fell from No. 1 to No. 7 in the AP poll, putting more attention on an offense that hasn't consistently met expectations.

Sarkisian has defended Manning against criticism tied to his famous last name, arguing that his successes deserve more recognition. Young's view goes further by questioning the play-calling around him.

Of course, Manning still has the rest of 2026 to work through those issues at Texas, and his plans for 2027 remain unknown. A move to Indiana would require several decisions that haven't been made.

That's what makes Young's prediction interesting rather than actionable: It's a statement about what Indiana's quarterback development might do for Manning, not evidence that he'll ever wear a Hoosiers uniform.

articles.title: Dave Roberts, Blake Snell lose after 7th-inning collapse
articles.summary: Blake Snell was dominating Game 3 of the NLCS. Until he wasn’t.
articles.body:
It's a tale as old as time: An All-Star left-handed starter for the Los Angeles Dodgers is dominating in a playoff start until it gets to the 7th inning. He throws a lot of pitches, maybe gets a little tired, and meanwhile Dave Roberts or Don Mattingly leaves him until disaster strikes.

Usually, that pitcher is Clayton Kershaw . Now that Kershaw has retired to focus on broadcasting a reclaiming the symbol of the rainbow, the burden of being Roberts' victim has fallen on one-year San Francisco Giants sensation Blake Snell.

In the 7th inning of the Dodgers' 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers, Snell was cruising along through six innings. After giving up a home run to Jackson Chourio on the first pitch of the game, Snell gave up only one more hit in the next six innings, retiring 14 Brewers in a row at one point. Then he walked Andrew Vaughn on seven pitches. Then, Jake Bauers started fouling pitches off.

Bauers fought off five two-strike pitches before going deep on Snell's 11th pitch of the at-bat, giving the Brewers a 3-2 advantage.

That took Snell's pitch count to 99. Though Snell is notorious for not going deep into games, Roberts chose to keep him in to face the left-handed Garrett Mitchell, even though a lefty had just taken Snell deep. It took only two more pitches for Roberts to regret his inaction.

It was immediately reminiscent of the 2019 Division Series between the Dodgers and Washington Nationals, when Kershaw came out of the bullpen and gave up back-to-back homers to Anthony Rendon and Juan Soto, the second another lefty-on-lefty matchup.

The common thread is that Roberts simply doesn't trust his bullpen in October a lot of the time. He may have been right to, since relievers Rory Sasaki and Justin Wrobleski let two more runs score in the 8th and 9th innings. Last season, Roberts got through a rough start by Shohei Ohtani in Game 7 of the World Series by using four starting pitchers in relief, including Snell, with Wrobleski the only full-time reliever entering the game.

Snell had some control issues in his first playoff start, walking five Atlanta Braves in 3.2 innings, though he only gave up one run. With the Dodgers trailing 3-0 in the series, he and Roberts may not get a chance to redeem themselves before the 2027 season.

Note: Snell may be in his second season pitching for the Dodgers, but the Giants still had to pay him $17M this year thanks to a deferred signing bonus from his 2024 contract. Maybe that's the reason he collapsed in the biggest moment. Simply getting a check from the 2026 Giants is enough to taint anyone in baseball with their 97-loss stink.

articles.title: Breece Hall remains sidelined Thursday
articles.summary: Jets RB Breece Hall on track to miss another game after two DNPs
articles.body:
New York Jets RB Breece Hall (quadriceps) did not participate in practice Thursday, Oct. 15.

Why It Matters: Hall seems likely to be at least a week away from returning to the lineup, so fantasy players can continue to avoid him for now. Braelon Allen will likely receive another start in Week 6 and can be a No. 3 running back or flex option in fantasy leagues.

articles.title: Seahawks elevate pair of newcomers from practice squad for Broncos game
articles.summary: The special teams gunner is set to make his debut with Seattle.
articles.body:
Through the first month of the season, the Seattle Seahawks struggled with kickoff coverage and rank near the bottom of the league in yards allowed per return, but they're set to gain a key special teams asset ahead of a crucial Week 6 road matchup against the Denver Broncos.

The team announced they've elevated wide receiver and special teams gunner Irv Charles, as well as linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo from the practice squad. Both will make their team debuts.

Acquired from the New York Jets in May , Charles missed the first five games while on injured reserve with a knee issue but was designated to return to practice on October 7. Seattle activated him to the active roster on Tuesday , although, he was released a day later to make room for running back Velus Jones Jr . As a vested veteran, Charles wasn't subject to waivers and rerouted to the practice squad.

Upon his return, Charles is expected to play a key role on kick and punt returns—areas where he's highly regarded.

On the defensive side, Ciarlo's elevation was expected given the Seahawks will be without starting linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) and Chazz Surratt (chest), leaving a thin group even thinner.

The third year linebacker went undrafted out of Army in 2024 before signing with the Jets, but missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury. He was released in May, 2025 and spent time with the Buffalo Bills, Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans prior to signing with the Seahawks on September 30.

articles.title: Texas A&M baseball releases complete 2027 schedule
articles.summary: Texas A&M’s 2027 schedule features five home SEC series, the BRUCE BOLT College Classic and a road series against Texas.
articles.body:
Texas A&M baseball released its complete 2027 schedule Wednesday, giving fans their first look at the path Michael Earley's team will face during his third season in College Station.

The Aggies will open the season with a three-game series at Blue Bell Park from Feb. 19-21. Their early nonconference schedule includes several home games before they travel to Houston for the BRUCE BOLT College Classic at Daikin Park. A&M will face Louisville on March 5, Louisiana on March 6 and Houston on March 7. The Aggies then return home for a midweek game and a three-game series against Loyola Marymount before opening SEC play.

Texas A&M begins its conference schedule at Alabama from March 19-21. The Aggies' five home SEC series will come against Tennessee, Oklahoma, LSU, Arkansas and Ole Miss.

The Oklahoma series should be one of the most anticipated weekends at Blue Bell Park. The Sooners are the defending national champions and haven't played in College Station since the programs were in the Big 12. A&M's conference road schedule includes trips to Alabama, Kentucky, Mississippi State, South Carolina and Texas. The Lone Star Showdown will be played May 14-16 in Austin before the Aggies close the regular season against Ole Miss from May 20-22.

The SEC Tournament is scheduled for May 25-30 at Hoover Metropolitan Stadium in Alabama.

The schedule will test a roster featuring 29 newcomers and only 15 returning letterwinners. Earley also enters the season with a new pitching coach in Barry Enright and associate head coach Nolan Cain back in College Station. Fall exhibitions against Rice and McNeese give the staff its first opportunities to evaluate the rebuilt roster before the Aggies begin their 2027 season in February.

Contact/Follow us @AggiesWire on X and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Texas A&M news, notes, and opinions. Follow Jarrett Johnson on X: @whosnextsports1 .

articles.title: Angel Reese, Gabby Williams headline WNBA All-Defensive team: Full list
articles.summary: The 2026 WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will feature six of the 10 players named to the WNBA All-Defensive teams.
articles.body:
The 2026 WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will feature six of 10 players named to the WNBA All-Defensive teams. Yes, you read that right.

Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese followed up her 2026 Defensive Player of the Year award with first-team All-Defensive honors, the WNBA announced on Thursday, Oct. 15. Reese is joined by Dream teammates Rhyne Howard and Jordin Canada, who earned first and second team honors, respectively.

The Dream's trio of defensive superstars will go head-to-head in the WNBA Finals against the Valkyries, who have their own trio of All-Defensive players. Valkyries forward Gabby Williams , who finished second in DPOY voting behind Reese, was named to the first team for the second consecutive season. Guard Veronica Burton and center Kiah Stokes were named to the second team.

Here are the WNBA players named to the 2026 WNBA All-Defensive teams:

Liberty, Dream and Aces, Valkyries in WNBA semifinal playoff action

Washington Mystics C Shakira Austin : The 6-foot-5 center anchored the league's top rebounding team, with the Mystics averaging 37.7 rebounds per game. Austin ranked second in the league in defensive rebounds (7.6) and fourth in total rebounds (9.5). She joins A'ja Wilson and Jonquel Jones as the only three players to average at least nine rebounds and one block this season.

Atlanta Dream G Rhyne Howard : The 6-foot-2 guard led the league in steals per game (2.3), setting a Dream single-season record (99) for steals in the process. Howard recorded three or more steals in 19 games this season, including two six-steal outings. Howard ranked third in the league in defensive win shares (3.2).

Atlanta Dream F Angel Reese : Reese, the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year , picked up her first All-Defensive nod. The 6-foot-4 forward led the league in rebounds (12.1), offensive rebounds per game (4.8) and defensive win shares (3.4), while setting WNBA single-season records for total rebounds (521), total offensive rebounds (206) and double-doubles (32). Reese averaged a career-high 1.8 steals per game, which ranked third in the league behind Dream teammates Howard and Canada (1.9).

Golden State Valkyries F Gabby Williams : The 5-foot-11 forward finished second in DPOY voting for the second consecutive season after ranking second in the league in defensive NET points (25) and fifth in steals per game (1.6). The 2025 first-team All-Defensive pick has recorded three or more steals in eight games this season. Williams, who played for France, was named the Best Defensive Player at the FIBA Women's World Cup.

Las Vegas Aces C A'ja Wilson : The 6-foot-4 center was named All-Defense for the seventh season straight. Wilson led the league in total blocks (79), blocks per game (1.9) and steals and blocks per game (3.3). She recorded a season-high five blocks in the Aces' 79-69 win over the Los Angeles Sparks on June 2, where she added 25 points and 15 rebounds to her stat line. The 2026 WNBA MVP has recorded three or more blocks in 10 games this season and grabbed 15 rebounds in five games. She finished third in the league in defensive rebounds (7.5) and fifth in rebounds per game (9.4).

Golden State Valkyries G Veronica Burton : The 5-foot-9 guard led the league in defensive win shares (.212) and defensive NET points (29), all while averaging a career-high 1.6 steals per game, which is tied for fifth in the league. It marks Burton's second consecutive WNBA All-Defensive second-team honor.

Golden State Valkyries C Kiah Stokes : The 6-foot-3 center ranked second in the league in total blocks (74) and fourth in the league in blocks per game (1.7). Stokes recorded three or more blocks in 11 games this season and five or more blocks in three contests. She had season-high seven blocks in the Valkyries' win over the Atlanta Dream on June 26.

Washington Mystics G Sonia Citron : The 6-foot-1 guard averaged 1.2 steals and 0.6 blocks in her sophomore season. She recorded three games with three or more steals, including a five-steal outing in the Mystics' win over the New York Liberty on June 19. She also had five games this season with two or more blocks. Citron became the first guard in franchise history to record 150 rebounds, 45 steals and 25 blocks in a single season.

Atlanta Dream G Jordin Canada : The 5-foot-6 guard finished second in the league with 1.9 steals per game, finishing behind her Dream teammate Rhyne Howard. Canada recorded 14 games this season with three or more steals, including a season-high seven steals in the Dream's loss to the Las Vegas Aces on May 17.

New York Liberty F Breanna Stewart : The 2026 WNBA Commissioner's Cup MVP is leading the Liberty in points (19.2), steals (1.4) and blocks (1.3) in her 10th season in the league, while ranking second in rebounds (8.5). Stewart has scored double-digits in all but one game this season and her seven double-doubles is tied for the fifth-most in the league. Stewart has been named All-Defense eight times.

articles.title: ‘Loyal to your soil’: Fans celebrate Sacramento Kings at annual Fan Fest
articles.summary: (FOX40.COM) — Grab your snacks, your dancing shoes and your Sacramento spirit, because Wednesday night at the Golden 1 Center, fans across the region joined...
articles.body:
(FOX40.COM) -- Grab your snacks, your dancing shoes and your Sacramento spirit, because Wednesday night at the Golden 1 Center, fans across the region joined together for the Sacramento Kings' annual Fan Fest and open practice.

While many community members were there to celebrate basketball, this special event puts the fans in the spotlight.

"I haven't been to a Kings game in years," a fan, James, said. "I want to come figure out who the new team is now."

Seas of purple took over the night as fans united under one roof to showcase their pride and dedication.

"You have to be loyal to your soil," one fan told FOX40. "You're in Sacramento. You've got to represent your city. You've got to stay loyal no matter what -- light the beam!"

FOX40 asked fans what they are most excited for this season and what they love most about the Kings and Fan Fest.

"The game," one fan said. "Zach LaVine, the game ... definitely the game. The excitement for the city, the game, the amazing dancers. It's just always lit. It's a good time."

"My favorite thing about the Sacramento Kings is when we light the beam," another fan screamed out.

Some fans said other elements of the team stood out the most.

"The color purple," one fan said when asked what she loves most about the team.

And for James, the sport itself is the focal point of Wednesday's event.

"Basketball, I love basketball," James said regarding his loyalty to the team.

"I'm excited to see everybody play, all the new players [to begin]," a fan named Susan said alongside her family. "We want to see the dance off, gotta love it, them dancing. I want to see what the new players' moves are."

From names on jerseys to entertainment on the courts, this fan fest was about supporting your team.

Fans like Ryder Gillespie said the Kings have a special place in their hearts.

"I've kind of started picking up basketball because of the Kings," Gillespie said. "It's been great. I've been a fan ever since I was a kid, so, I come out here every year and it's just really fun."

Some fans are new, others have been here since before Slamson and the color purple.

"If you're going to be true, be true to it," James said. "I was here since ARCO, so I've been a fan for that many years."

Attendees enjoyed free snacks, discounted merch and a chance to support Sutter Health patients, all while smiling with one another and building up their anticipation for the new season ahead.

"The fans are great," Gillespie said. "It's great out here. I love all the new faces, everything."

The Kings first regular season game against the Los Angeles Clippers kicks off next Wednesday.

articles.title: Stayton football forfeits game with rival Cascade
articles.summary: Stayton football has forfeited its Week 7 game against Cascade. It's another in a growing trend in Oregon high school football.
articles.body:
Another Oregon high school football team has forfeited a varsity game.

On Oct. 15, just a day before kickoff against rival Cascade in Turner, Stayton has forfeited the Week 7 conference game.

"The contest was forfeited because a team did not have enough participants in order to play. The team forfeited prior to competition; the contest was never started. Forfeit posted by OSAA on 10/15/2026," reads a message on the Oregon School Activities Association scoreboard.

The Statesman Journal reached out to Stayton High School but was unable to reach the principal, athletic director or football coach for comment.

Cascade, the reigning 4A state champion, loses a matchup with one of its biggest rivals in the heart of the season.

"We got word yesterday that they were concerned about their roster and the health of their roster, so there was communication between superintendents about that," Cascade athletic director and football coach Shane Hedrick said Oct. 15. "Today they called and said due to those concerns, they'd be withdrawing their teams for both varsity and JV."

The varsity game between the two schools was scheduled for Oct. 16 and the junior varsity game for Oct. 19.

"We totally understand the safety of the game and respect that," Hedrick added. "This game is so strong in this community in this era. And it's senior night for us ... but the underlying thing is that the game has to be safe, we totally agree to that."

According to the OSAA website, the Eagles have 35 players on the varsity roster. Prior to this week, the Eagles were on a two-game losing streak but hold a 3-3 overall record and Class 4A's No. 21 overall ranking.

Stayton is not the first Willamette Valley football team to have cancelled a game, or season, this fall. Back in early September, 3A's Blanchet Catholic cancelled its varsity season due to low numbers after two games.

Down Interstate 5, 5A school South Eugene cancelled its varsity season nearly a week before opening kickoff.

In the same conference as Stayton and Cascade this week, a game between Central/Kings Valley Charter and Gladstone/Riverdale was forfeited due to "not enough participants in order to play," according to the OSAA.

Gladstone/Riverdale has also already forfeited its Week 9 game against Cascade, Hedrick said.

Cascade's next scheduled varsity game is Oct. 23 at home against McKay. Stayton's varsity team is scheduled to host Philomath on Oct. 23.

There have been several more one-game forfeits and season cancellations across Oregon this fall. It's a growing trend that's now reached into Class 4A's Special District 2.
